locationCostEstimate.historicalContext: All costs are estimated based on production standards and values of the mid-1960s.

processingEvidence.summary: Calculated fees for 3 practical African locations and a long-term studio lease. Factored in prep/hold periods for extensive set builds.

practicalLocationFees.description: Block booking fee for exclusive access to African plains, stream, and cave exterior locations for the duration of the Africa shoot block (~25 days).

studioRentalFees.description: Long-term lease of multiple sound stages and ancillary facilities (workshops, offices, backlot) at a major UK studio (e.g., MGM-British Studios) for approximately 12 months to accommodate extensive prep, shoot, and strike.

governmentLiaisonFees.description: Fees for a dedicated local fixer/liaison in Africa to negotiate access, fees, and manage community relations.

processingEvidence.summary: Calculated international and domestic permit costs, including special clearances for construction and animal handling.

internationalPermits.description: Governmental filming permits, national park access fees, and environmental clearances for shooting in Africa.

animalWelfarePermits.description: Special permits for the use of a trained lion and other wildlife, including oversight from humane organizations.

constructionAndSafetyPermits.description: Fees for engineering review, safety certification, and regulatory approval for unprecedented set construction, particularly the rotating centrifuge.

processingEvidence.summary: Assessed and costed security for both high-risk remote locations and high-confidentiality studio sets.

remoteLocationSecurity.description: Team of local security personnel for 24/7 base camp and equipment protection in Africa, including wildlife perimeter control.

studioSecurity.description: Enhanced 24/7 security for the studio complex, including strict access control for stages with confidential sets (Discovery, Monolith) and high-value equipment.

processingEvidence.summary: Factored in costs for site restoration, damage bonds, and large-scale set striking.

practicalLocationRestoration.description: Cost of cleanup crew and environmental remediation to return African locations to their original state ('leave no trace'). Includes non-refundable portion of damage bond.

studioSetStrikeAndCleanup.description: Labor and disposal costs for the complete teardown and removal of all large-scale sets (Centrifuge, Space Station, Moon Base, etc.) and restoration of studio stages.

processingEvidence.summary: Calculated costs for establishing a remote base camp and managing high-demand studio utilities.

remoteBaseCampFacilities.description: Rental and setup of a full base camp in Africa, including generators, water bowsers, mobile toilets, catering tents, and staging areas.

studioPowerAndUtilities.description: Significant utility costs for powering massive sets, especially the rotating centrifuge mechanism and extensive lighting grids, over the entire production period.

studioParkingAndSupport.description: Costs for overflow parking for a large crew and management of ancillary support areas within the studio lot.

locationCostSummary.summaryNotes: Total reflects the immense scale of the production, dominated by the cost of pioneering custom set construction. The high-end of the confidence interval accounts for significant R&D and technical challenges inherent in the project's design.

breakdown.notes: Includes national filming permits and animal welfare clearances.
Essential for navigating local logistics and regulations.
24/7 protection for crew, cast, and equipment in a remote environment.
Power, water, shelter, and sanitation for the entire Africa unit.
Long-term package deal for multiple stages, workshops, and offices.
The largest single location-related expense. See sub-breakdown.

subBreakdown.details: Design, engineering, construction, and operation of the 38-foot diameter, 30-ton rotating set. A pioneering and costly piece of infrastructure.
Includes the large Clavius Base conference room, reception, airlocks, and the multi-level Tycho excavation set with lunar surface effects.
Construction of multiple high-fidelity cockpits, passenger areas, pod bays, and the Discovery command module and brain room.
Construction of the reception area, Hilton lounge, and restaurant sets with integrated viewscreens and futuristic furniture.
Includes the Stargate slit-scan rig, model photography stages, and the final 'Hotel Room' set.

breakdown.notes: High consumption due to set mechanics and extensive lighting.
Labor and disposal for all constructed sets.
Freight, carnets, and brokerage for shipping equipment to and from Africa.
Pre-production travel and surveys for both international and potential domestic locations.

riskAssessmentAndContingency.notes: A substantial contingency is allocated due to the unprecedented technical and logistical risks of the production.

riskFactors.description: Failure or delay of the custom-built centrifuge mechanism.
riskFactors.mitigation: Allocate contingency funds for extended R&D, on-site engineers, and potential rebuilds. Schedule buffer already in place.

riskFactors.description: Weather or logistical delays during the Africa shoot impacting the master schedule.
riskFactors.mitigation: Contingency funds for extra days, transport, or securing alternative sub-locations.

riskFactors.description: Cost overruns in materials and labor for massive set construction due to the novelty and scale of the designs.
riskFactors.mitigation: Contingency covers potential increases in raw material prices and specialized labor rates.

riskFactors.description: Regulatory hurdles or safety compliance issues with novel set designs.
riskFactors.mitigation: Budget for additional consultants and potential modifications required by authorities.

alternativeLocationOptions.option: Simulate Africa in a controlled environment
alternativeLocationOptions.description: Use a large backlot or a location like the Canary Islands or southern Spain to replicate African landscapes. Build cave sets entirely in-studio.
alternativeLocationOptions.pros: Greater control over weather, logistics, and animal handling. Reduced company move costs and security risks.
alternativeLocationOptions.cons: May lack the authentic scale and lighting of the African plains. Potential for higher construction costs to replicate nature.

alternativeLocationOptions.option: Consolidate all construction in a US studio
alternativeLocationOptions.description: Base the entire studio portion of the shoot in Hollywood instead of the UK.
alternativeLocationOptions.pros: Proximity to top-tier VFX houses and specialized engineering talent of the era.
alternativeLocationOptions.cons: Potentially higher labor and studio rental costs compared to the UK in the 1960s. Loss of potential UK tax incentives/Eady Levy benefits.
